subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What should the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary be across agents and channels: bot-account scoped, resolved-agent/session scoped, tenant-aware, channel/chat provenance, or explicit-share based?
rationale: The issue is security-sensitive and changing the media path/reference contract without maintainer intent could either leave isolation gaps or break existing managed-media references and staging behavior.

options.title: Define Scoped Contract First
options.body: Choose the ownership identity, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation touches storage and staging paths.

options.title: Limit To Account Scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model while accepting that non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant-sharing cases may need follow-up.

options.title: Defer Broad Core Change
options.body: Keep only channel-specific slices open until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel core media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define Scoped Contract First
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership identity, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation touches storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and recently maintained central inbound media/staging behavior and previously reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
